newsitem.title: CHINA: China banks not threatened by foreign bank growth.
newsitem.headline: China banks not threatened by foreign bank growth.

text.p: Foreign banks chosen to do Chinese yuan business are unlikely to pose a threat to China's domestic banks because of the strict limits placed upon them, the China Daily Business Weekly reported on Sunday.

The newspaper quoted an official with the People's Bank of China, the central bank, as saying the foreign banks would complement the role played by the Chinese banks in serving foreign-invested enterprises in Shanghai.
"The move will have little impact on domestic banks because of limits imposed on the volume of yuan business handled by the foreign banks," the newspaper quoted the official as saying.
The four banks chosen in late December to do local currency business are the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp, Citibank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank and the Industrial Bank of Japan.

Operations have not yet started due to a lack of detailed regulations and because of the central bank's ruling that the foreign banks first move their main operations to the Pudong area east of Shanghai's city centre, bankers say.

"The proportion of local currency loans to foreign-funded enterprises in the lending portfolio of domestic banks in Shanghai has failed to accommodate the business growth of foreign ventures in the city," the central bank official said.
"Now the pilot foreign banks can complement domestic banks to help make up the shortage of local currency loans to foreign ventures," he added.
But he said the experimental programme would increase competition for domestic banks, albeit on a limited scale, thereby encouraging the Chinese banks to improve their performance.
The foreign banks, up to now restricted to doing foreign currency business, will generally only be allowed to take in deposits or make loans to foreign-invested enterprises based in Shanghai.
Foreign bankers say funding is expected to be a major problem as foreign-invested enterprises generally don't have large quantities of Chinese yuan that they wish to place on deposit.
